summary: Default /z-plan intent-compiler and adaptive INTENT execution model: /z-plan compiles conversation into INTENT.md plus an initial append-only known-work graph (work-graph.json), and /z-execute freezes INTENT then schedules over that graph via task-tree-generator (now a known-work graph expander) with LEDGER checkpoints and durable-DAG-settle-point acceptance evaluation.

entry_points.summary: Validate frontmatter and required sections by intent level.
Lint non-observable acceptance checklist criteria.
Set frozen_at back to pending for amended contracts.
Stamp frozen_at idempotently; reports FROZEN or ALREADY_FROZEN.
Create LEDGER.md frontmatter if absent without overwriting existing content.
Evaluate checklist criteria from INTENT, LEDGER citations, and cumulative diff.
scheduler_mode: known_work_graph makes the generator append nodes to work_graph_path instead of only emitting a flat batch.
Append only work knowable from INTENT/flags/graph/last outcome; placeholder nodes must be explicit and sparing.

entry_points.symbol: Phase 2 — Emit TASKS.md and append the graph
entry_points.summary: Appends stable-ID nodes (T/W prefix), sets status=ready only when depends_on are done, appends append_log entry.
/z-plan default path is conversation -> sharpened problem -> optional ideated framing -> intent contract -> execution DAG; full SDD is explicit compatibility only.
/z-plan must run shared /z-sharpen inline or consume fresh GRILL.md before planning.
/z-plan asks whether to run /z-brainstorm and may recommend it when alternatives remain; it never auto-dispatches brainstorm.
After sharpen and optional brainstorm artifacts stabilize, /z-plan evaluates the shared compaction/checkpoint seam before high-context planning.
/z-plan restates the sharpened problem/framing, grounds only missing source facts, drafts INTENT.md, and iterates with the user 1-2 times.

entry_points.symbol: concern flags plus optional audit ask
entry_points.summary: Before final read-through, /z-plan surfaces LLM concern/decision/assumption flags and asks whether to fold in /z-audit-plan.

Phase 8 writes the initial work-graph.json known-work frontier (~line 2622), then derives execution-strategy.md (~line 2713) from TASKS.md + work-graph.json + workstreams.json; hard-fails if work-graph.json is missing.
After execution strategy and handoff artifacts stabilize, /z-plan evaluates the shared checkpoint seam before /z-execute.
SPEC.md present -> legacy; INTENT.md present -> intent; neither -> halt.
Freeze INTENT and snapshot to archive/INTENT.frozen.md on first freeze.
Resolves work-graph.json via the same exact-name _resolve_exact_plan_artifact seam as other intent-conversation companions.
Re-reads work-graph.json, computes the ready frontier, dispatches via the reusable per-task engine, refills/appends as nodes return.
Expands known-work graph and refreshes TASKS.md projection for the current frontier.
Injects intent_snapshot:, ledger_path:, and (when present) work_graph_path: into implementer/reviewer prompts.
After each settled frontier, recomputes node status from TASKS.md markers and depends_on; appends status_log entry.
Marks TASKS.md stale so task-tree-generator regenerates after amended contract.

invariants: /z-plan default mode is an intent compiler; legacy full SDD is explicit compatibility only.
Sharpening is the first planning phase: /z-plan runs the shared /z-sharpen inline contract or consumes fresh GRILL.md before INTENT drafting.
Brainstorm is a user ask gate: /z-plan may recommend /z-brainstorm but never auto-dispatches it.
INTENT.md is drafted through a short user iteration loop before final approval.
Concern flags are surfaced before final read-through, and /z-plan asks whether to incorporate an optional /z-audit-plan scan.
Execution strategy metadata includes task-to-intent mapping, safe parallel batches, serial blockers, review gates, checkpoint cadence, and workstream/handoff data.

work-graph.json is the durable append-only known-work DAG: /z-plan seeds the initial frontier from TASKS.md; /z-execute appends nodes via task-tree-generator (scheduler_mode: known_work_graph) and never deletes/rewrites existing node identity or append_log entries.

task-tree-generator may widen a ready frontier only when siblings have precise disjoint file scope and executor fan-out can be capped or partitioned; otherwise it must connect work with explicit graph dependencies (depends_on) rather than broadening the ready set.
Watcher checkpoint seams run after preplanning artifacts and after execution strategy/handoff artifacts stabilize.
Unknown acceptance state counts as unmet.
workflow.intent_parallel_levels defaults true but controls within-frontier sibling dispatch only, under /z-execute safety preconditions.

True node-by-node pipelined refill (dispatching another ready node without draining the current frontier) is permitted only when the driver exposes a durable background handle/completion notification per track; synchronous-only hosts must drain-then-refill and must not report telemetry as concurrently refilled when they did not.
gotchas: workflow.intent_bfs_level_cap is runtime-read and may not appear in DEFAULTS; empty/None falls back to 6.
stale_reason: amended-intent must replace any existing key, not duplicate it.
.bfs_level_state hash mismatch restarts from scheduler depth 0; in known-work-graph mode it is a resume/telemetry hint only, not the source of scheduling truth.
Brainstorm and audit are ask gates, not automatic route changes: /z-plan can recommend /z-brainstorm or /z-audit-plan, but it never launches them.
Execution strategy metadata is part of the planning contract consumed by fresh /z-execute context; do not treat TASKS.md alone as the complete handoff.
Do not pass spec_path/plan_path to implementers in INTENT mode.
Missing, unparseable, overlapping, or scope_unknown same-frontier task scope serializes the affected node/frontier via an explicit depends_on edge; do not infer arbitrary fan-out.

Default-on workflow.intent_parallel_levels still requires precise Files scope, bounded/partitioned fan-out (INTENT_PARALLEL_FANOUT_LIMIT, hardcoded 3), and per-task review diff isolation or serialized review capture.

work-graph.json node identity and append_log[] are append-only, but the status field IS mutable scheduler state, resynced by /z-execute after every settled frontier (skills/z-execute/SKILL.md:1150) from TASKS.md task markers.
execution-strategy.md generation now hard-fails (SystemExit) if work-graph.json is missing after Phase 8's work-graph write.
WORK_GRAPH_FILE resolution mirrors intent-conversation companion artifacts: exact-name lookup via _resolve_exact_plan_artifact, never a fuzzy archive scan, falling back to $BASE/work-graph.json.
Current native hosts only issue synchronous Agent() calls, so true node-by-node pipelined refill is contract-only for them; they still drain a full frontier before refilling.

config_keys.workflow.planning_mode: intent|full recommendation for the explicit mode gate
config_keys.workflow.intent_level: auto|quick|standard|deep; level flags override and bypass classifier
config_keys.workflow.intent_parallel_levels: bool, default true; opt out with false; same-frontier INTENT parallelism only when /z-execute safety preconditions pass
config_keys.workflow.hermes_enabled: bool master gate for Hermes machinery

memories.text: When INTENT acceptance promises DAG/workstream metadata, generator failure must halt or surface clearly; prose fallback/||true silently erases the execution contract.
In adaptive INTENT BFS, later task-tree generation must receive concern flags, brainstorm choice, execution strategy, and task-to-intent/workstream context before tasks are drafted.

For adaptive INTENT execution, aggregate review is a computed gate: log required/not-required from realized task count, workstreams, high-risk flags, and cross-workstream criteria; do not replace it with unconditional final review.

Load-bearing intent-conversation artifacts must be resolved through stable plan-root pointers or exact handoff references, never by scanning archives for the latest matching flags or brainstorm choice.

The brainstorm ask gate needs a durable route/choice artifact with skipped, existing, and routed states, and later /z-plan resumes must consume that artifact deterministically before drafting INTENT.md.
